script.text: Iran just said no talks with Washington. So who stops the next strike?

Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, flew to Tehran on Tuesday. Reuters counts it as his fifth visit since the April ceasefire. He also met the foreign minister and the parliament speaker. He is trying to restart talks between Iran and the US.

Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian, told him Washington must first lift sanctions and end its threats. He said Iranians fear talks will be followed by another attack. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei added that not one gram of enriched uranium will leave Iran.

Parliament speaker Mohammad Ghalibaf says trust needs seven conditions, including an end to the US blockade of Iranian ports. Those are also Iran's terms for reopening Hormuz. The reports show no US reply yet.
Will Iran and the US sit down by December? Yes or no?

upload.title: Iran to Pakistan: No Talks With the US Yet #shorts
upload.description:
Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran on October 20 to try to revive US-Iran talks; Reuters counts it as his fifth visit to Iran since the April ceasefire that Islamabad brokered. According to Iranian reports, Pezeshkian said the United States must lift sanctions and end threats before any negotiations, and that Iranians fear talks would be followed by another attack. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said no enriched uranium will be removed from Iran. Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Washington cannot win Tehran's trust until it meets seven conditions set last month for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, including an end to the US blockade of Iranian ports and sanctions relief on oil exports. The reports reviewed contained no US response.
